=== Formal Public Comment - PUCT Docket 59475 (Link G31 - Darian Stern).pdf ===
PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS


DOCKET NO. 59475

APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA
TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF
CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE PROPOSED BELL COUNTY EAST TO BIG
HILL 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE PROJECT
FORMAL PUBLIC COMMENT OF DARIAN STERN​
REGARDING ROUTE LINK G31 (TRACT 2168 / US HIGHWAY 183 CORRIDOR)


TO THE HONORABLE PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION OF TEXAS:


I am submitting this formal public comment to urge the Commission and the presiding
Administrative Law Judge to reject Link G31 due to critical, unaddressed conflicts with
statutory community values, public safety, and active emergency response infrastructure
under Texas Utilities Code (PURA) § 37.056(c)(4) and 16 TAC § 25.101(b)(3)(B).


The Applicants' Environmental Assessment improperly categorizes Tract 2168 and the
adjacent US Highway 183 frontage as unimproved, vacant agricultural pasture. This
desktop characterization fails to reflect actual land use, local public assembly, and
emergency operations:


   1.​ Elimination of an Irreplaceable Community Resource (PURA § 37.056(c)(4)):
   ●​ Link G31 bisects Tract 2168, cutting directly across the designated launch grounds
       and spectator assembly area of the annual Briggs/Oakalla Community
       Independence Day Celebration.
   ●​ This civic event has operated continuously at this specific parcel since 2019,
       serving as a primary gathering for hundreds of rural families across southern Bell
       and northern Burnet Counties.
   ●​ Due to mandatory safety clearances, required explosive fallout radiuses away
       from surrounding residences, highway sightlines, and necessary proximity to the
       fire department for fire-watch apparatus, no other viable public site exists in the
      Briggs/Oakalla area to host this event.
   ●​ Constructing a 765-kV transmission line carrying 155- to 190-foot structures and
      a 200-foot right-of-way easement directly through this parcel will permanently
      extinguish this community tradition due to high-voltage arc-flashover risks,
      projectile collision hazards, and standard utility safety restrictions prohibiting
      large public gatherings and ignition sources within extra-high-voltage
      easements.
   2.​ Severe Hazards to Emergency Response and Medevac Airspace:
   ●​ Immediately south of Tract 2168, Link G31 crosses US Highway 183 directly
      adjacent to the Northeast Burnet County Fire Rescue station apron.
   ●​ In prior Commission proceedings involving local transmission routing (e.g.,
      Docket No. 37463), the applicant explicitly inventoried rural volunteer fire
      department grounds as protected aviation facilities and emergency medical
      helicopter landing zones (EMS Heliports) subject to mandatory clearance slopes.
   ●​ Suspending uninsulated 765-kV conductors and catenary ground wires across
      US-183 in front of the station creates an immediate vertical and visual barrier for
      emergency aeromedical evacuation helicopters (such as Travis County STAR
      Flight and military medevac units) attempting low-altitude, visual landings on
      the highway or station apron during vehicular crashes, wildland fire responses,
      and community emergencies.
   ●​ Furthermore, the proximity of the proposed towers directly compromises ground
      staging and rapid deployment of emergency apparatus exiting onto US-183.
   3.​ Routing Deficiency in the Applicant's Study:
   ●​ The Applicants failed to identify this active public gathering ground and
      emergency response envelope during their preliminary constraint mapping,
      presenting the Commission with flawed routing metric comparisons that
      undercount the true human and safety impacts of Link G31.


Under PURA § 37.056, the Commission is statutorily bound to protect community values,
recreational resources, and public safety. Because Link G31 destroys an irreplaceable
community event and creates hazardous overhead obstructions at an active rural fire
station, Link G31 must be eliminated from further consideration in Docket No. 59475.
 Respectfully submitted,


Darian Stern​
Briggs, Texas​
https://www.facebook.com/BriggsOakallaFireworks/
Attachments: Photographic documentation of the Briggs/Oakalla Community Independence
Day gathering on Tract 2168, including (1) a wide field view showing spectator vehicles and the
open horizon along the proposed Link G31 centerline, and (2) an elevated patio/pavilion view
showing families, children, picnic tables, food tents, and the full crowd density and vehicle
parking directly on Tract 2168.
